1000.subject: Chemistry
1000.text: How many litres of ammonia gas at S.T.P. would be needed to prepare $100 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $2.5 \mathrm{M}$ ammonium hydroxide solution?
1000.sol:
Molecular weight of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}=35$
Now, $35 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ is needed to prepare $1 \mathrm{M}$ solution in 1 litre
$\Rightarrow 35 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH} in 1 \mathrm{~L}$ solution $\equiv 1$ molar solution
$\Rightarrow 2.5 \times 35 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ in $1 \mathrm{~L}$ solution $\equiv 2.5$ molar solution


\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow $\frac{2.5 \times 35}{10} \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH} \text{$ is } 100 $\mathrm{~mL} \text{ solution }$ \equiv 2.5 $\text{ molar solution }$ \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 8.75 $\mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH} \text{ was dissolved. }$ \\
& $\mathrm{NH}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ \rightarrow $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ \\
& \quad $\text{$ For } 35 $\mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$, $\mathrm{NH}_3 \text{ needed }=$22.4 $\mathrm{~L} \text{ at S.T.P }$ \\
& \Rightarrow \quad $\text{$ for } 8.75 $\mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$, $\mathrm{NH}_3 \text{ needed }=\frac{22.4}{35} \times$ 8.75 $\mathrm{~L}$ \\
&=5.6 $\mathrm{~L}$
\end{aligned}

1362.subject: Physics
1362.text: A uniform coil of self-inductance $1.8 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{H}$ and resistance $6 \Omega$ is broken up into two identical coils. These two coils are then connected in parallel across a $12 \mathrm{~V}$ battery. The circuit time constant and steady state current through the battery respectively are
1362.sol:
When coil is broken into two identical parts, then resistance of each part
$R^{\prime}=\frac{R}{2}=\frac{6}{2}=3 \Omega$
Inductance of each part
$L^{\prime}=\frac{L}{2}=\frac{1.8}{2} \times 10^{-4}=0.9 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{H}$
Now, time constant $\tau=\frac{L^{\prime}}{R^{\prime}}$
$\tau=\frac{L}{2 \times \frac{R}{2}}=\frac{L}{R}=\frac{1.8 \times 10^{-4}}{6}=30 \mu \mathrm{s}$
Now, effective resistance when both coils are connected in parallel
$R^{\prime \prime}=\frac{R^{\prime} \times R^{\prime}}{R^{\prime}+R^{\prime}}=\frac{3 \times 3}{3+3}=\frac{9}{6} \Omega$
So, maximum current drawn from battery
$I=\frac{V}{R^{\prime \prime}}=\frac{12}{9 / 6}=8 \mathrm{~A}$

3038.text: The equilibrium constant at $850 \mathrm{ K}$ for the reaction $\mathrm{N}_2(g)+\mathrm{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}(g)$ is 0.5625. The equilibrium concentration of $\mathrm{NO}(g)$ is $3.0 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$. If the equilibrium concentrations of $\mathrm{N}_2(g)$ and $\mathrm{O}_2(g)$ are equal, the concentrations of $\mathrm{N}_2(g)$ in $M$ is
3038.sol:
Given,
$\mathrm{N}_2(g)+\mathrm{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}(g)$
i.e. equilibrium constant, $K_C=0.5625$
Equilibrium concentration of $[\mathrm{NO}]=3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}\begin{array}{rlrl} & & K_C & =\frac{\left[\mathrm{NO}^2\right.}{\left[\mathrm{N}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]} \\
& \text{But, } & {\left[\mathrm{N}_2\right]} & =\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right] \quad \text{(Given)} \\
& \therefore & K_C & =\frac{[\mathrm{NO}]^2}{\left[\mathrm{ N}_2\right]^2} \\
& & & \\
\text{or, } & 0.5625 & =\frac{\left[3 \times 10^{-3}\right]^2}{\left[\mathrm{ N}_2\right]^2} \\
& \text{or, } & {\left[\mathrm{N}_2\right]^2} & =\frac{\left[3 \times 10^{-3}\right]^2}{0.5625}=\frac{9 \times 10^{-6}}{0.5625} \\
& \text{or, } & {\left[\mathrm{N}_2\right]^2} & =16 \times 10^{-6} \\
\text{or, } & {\left[\mathrm{N}_2\right]} & =4 \times 10^{-3}
\end{array}$
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

5820.sol:
According to the& Freundlich's Adsorption Isotherm,

$\dfrac{x}{m} = k \cdot p^{1 / n}$

By taking the log both sides,

$log\dfrac{x}{m} = logk + \dfrac{1}{n}logp$

So, slope $= \dfrac{1}{n} ⇒ tan45 ° = 1 ( n = 1 )$

$logK = 0 . 3010 ⇒ k = 2$

$\dfrac{x}{m} = 2( 0 . 5 )\dfrac{1}{n}\dfrac{x}{m} = 1$

Hence, the amount of gas adsorbed per gram of charcoal under a pressure of $0 . 5atm$ is $1 . 0g$

8558.text: The eccentric angle of a point on the ellipse $x^{2} + 3y^{2} = 6$ lying at a distance of $2$ units from its centre is
8558.sol:
The given equation of ellipse can be written in the form& $\dfrac{x2}{\left(\sqrt{6}\right)2} + \dfrac{y2}{\left(\sqrt{2}\right)2} = 1$.

Now let the eccentric angle of the point be~$\theta$, then its co-ordinates are~$\left(\sqrt{6}cos\theta, \sqrt{2}sin\theta\right)$.

Since the distance of the point from the centre is~$2$~units

$∴ \left(\sqrt{6}cos\theta - 0\right)2 + \left(\sqrt{2}sin\theta - 0\right)2 = 4$

$⇒ 6{cos}^{2}\theta + 2\left(1 - {cos}^{2}\theta\right) = 4 ⇒ 4{cos}^{2}\theta = 2$

$⇒ cos\theta = \pm \dfrac{1}{2} ∴ \theta = \dfrac{π}{4}$~or& $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

10603.subject: Mathematics
10603.text: In a consignment of 15 articles, it is found that 3 are defective. If a sample of 5 articles is chosen at random from it, then the probability of having 2 defective articles is
10603.sol:
Define the variables - Total articles $=15$ - Defective articles $=3$ - Non-defective articles $=15-3=12$ - Sample size $=5$ - We need the probability of choosing exactly 2 defective articles in this sample.
Use combinations to calculate possible outcomes The probability can be calculated using combinations, as we are dealing with a selection of items without regard to the order. 1. Number of ways to choose 2 defective articles out of 3: $\binom{3}{2}=\frac{3!}{2!(3-2)!}=3$ 2. Number of ways to choose 3 nondefective articles out of 12: $\binom{12}{3}=\frac{12!}{3!(12-3)!}=220$ 3. Total number of ways to choose 5 articles out of 15: $\binom{15}{5}=\frac{15!}{5!(15-5)!}=3003$
Calculate the probability The probability of selecting exactly 2 defective articles and 3 non-defective articles is: $\frac{\binom{3}{2} \times\binom{ 12}{3}}{\binom{15}{5}}=\frac{3 \times 220}{3003}=\frac{660}{3003}=\frac{128}{625}$
The probability of having exactly 2 defective articles in the sample is: $\frac{128}{625}$ So, the correct answer is $\frac{128}{625}$.

20144.subject: Chemistry
20144.text:
The conductivity of 0.01 M solution of $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ at 298 K is $1.65 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{Scm}^{-1}$
What is the $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ value of the acid if $\lambda^0 \left(\mathrm{H}^{+}\right)and \lambda^0\left(\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COO}\right)^{-1}$ are $349.1 \mathrm{Scm}^2 \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ and $40.9 \mathrm{Scm}^2 \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ respectively?
20144.sol:
The molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ is given by the formula $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa \times 1000}{C}$, where $\kappa = 1.65 \times 10^{-4} \text{ S cm}^{-1}$ and $C = 0.01 \text{ M}$.

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{1.65 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000}{0.01} = 16.5 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

The limiting molar conductivity $\Lambda_m^0$ is $\lambda^0(\text{H}^+) + \lambda^0(\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-) = 349.1 + 40.9 = 390.0 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

The degree of dissociation $\alpha$ is given by $\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^0} = \dfrac{16.5}{390.0} \approx 0.0423$.

The dissociation constant $K_a$ is given by $K_a = \dfrac{C\alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$. Since $\alpha$ is small, $1 - \alpha \approx 1$.

$K_a \approx C\alpha^2 = 0.01 \times (0.0423)^2 = 0.01 \times 0.001789 = 1.789 \times 10^{-5}$.

The $\text{pK}_a$ value is $-\log_{10}(K_a) = -\log_{10}(1.789 \times 10^{-5}) = 5 - \log_{10}(1.789) \approx 5 - 0.2526 = 4.747$.

Answer: $4.75$

22185.subject: Mathematics
22185.text: If the straight lines $\dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y-3}{1}=\dfrac{z-4}{-t}$ and $\dfrac{x-1}{t}=\dfrac{y-4}{2}=\dfrac{z-5}{1}$ are intersecting then $t$ can have
22185.sol:
The given lines are $L_1: \dfrac{x-2}{1} = \dfrac{y-3}{1} = \dfrac{z-4}{-t} = \lambda$ and $L_2: \dfrac{x-1}{t} = \dfrac{y-4}{2} = \dfrac{z-5}{1} = \mu$.

The general points on the lines are $P_1 = (2+\lambda, 3+\lambda, 4-t\lambda)$ and $P_2 = (1+t\mu, 4+2\mu, 5+\mu)$.

For the lines to intersect, there must exist $\lambda$ and $\mu$ such that $P_1 = P_2$. This gives the system of equations:

1) $2+\lambda = 1+t\mu \Rightarrow \lambda - t\mu = -1$

2) $3+\lambda = 4+2\mu \Rightarrow \lambda - 2\mu = 1$

3) $4-t\lambda = 5+\mu \Rightarrow t\lambda + \mu = -1$

Subtracting equation (2) from (1): $(-t+2)\mu = -2 \Rightarrow \mu = \dfrac{-2}{2-t} = \dfrac{2}{t-2}$.

Substituting $\mu$ into (2): $\lambda = 1 + 2\mu = 1 + \dfrac{4}{t-2} = \dfrac{t+2}{t-2}$.

Substituting $\lambda$ and $\mu$ into (3): $t\left(\dfrac{t+2}{t-2}\right) + \dfrac{2}{t-2} = -1$.

$t^2 + 2t + 2 = -(t-2) = -t + 2$.

$t^2 + 3t = 0 \Rightarrow t(t+3) = 0$.

The possible values for $t$ are $0$ and $-3$. Thus, there are exactly two values.

Answer: Exactly two values

22521.subject: Physics
22521.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
22521.text: Momentum of a body is increased to three times its original value. By what percentage will its kinetic energy change?
22521.sol:
The kinetic energy $K$ of a body is related to its momentum $p$ by the formula $K = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}$, where $m$ is the mass of the body.

Let the initial momentum be $p_1 = p$ and the initial kinetic energy be $K_1 = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}$.

The momentum is increased to three times its original value, so the new momentum is $p_2 = 3p$.

The new kinetic energy $K_2$ is given by $K_2 = \dfrac{p_2^2}{2m} = \dfrac{(3p)^2}{2m} = \dfrac{9p^2}{2m} = 9K_1$.

The change in kinetic energy is $\Delta K = K_2 - K_1 = 9K_1 - K_1 = 8K_1$.

The percentage change in kinetic energy is $\dfrac{\Delta K}{K_1} \times 100\% = \dfrac{8K_1}{K_1} \times 100\% = 800\%$.

Answer: $800 \%$

26077.text: A flat plate is moving normal to its plane through a gas under the action of a constant force F. The gas is kept at a very low pressure. The speed of the plate v I much less than the average speed u of the gas molecules. Which of the following options is true?
options: At a later time the external force F balances the resistive force
The resistive force experienced by the plate is proportional to v
The plate will continue to move with constant non zero acceleration at all times
The pressure difference between the leading and trailing faces of the plate is proportional to $uv$
26077.sol:
${v}_{1} = u + 2v$

${v}_{2} = \left(u - 2v\right)$

$\Delta{v}_{1} = \left(2u + 2v\right)$

$\Delta{v}_{2} = \left(2u - 2v\right)$

${F}_{1} = \dfrac{d{p}_{1}}{dt} = ρA\left(u + v\right)\left(2u + 2v\right)$

${F}_{2} = \dfrac{d{p}_{2}}{dt} = ρA\left(u - v\right)\left(2u - 2v\right)$

$= 2ρA{\left(u + v\right)}^{2}$

$= 2ρA{\left(u - v\right)}^{2}$

$\DeltaF = {F}_{1} - {F}_{2}$       ($\DeltaF$net force due to the air molecules on the plate)

$= 2ρA\left(4uv\right) = 8ρAuv$

$P = \dfrac{\DeltaF}{A} = 8ρ\left(uv\right)$

${F}_{net} = \left(F - \DeltaF\right) = ma$    (m is mass of the plate)

$F - \left(8ρAu\right)v = ma$

29652.text:
0.25 g of an organic compound " A " containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen was analysed using the combustion method. There was an increase in mass of $\mathrm{CaCl}_{2}$ tube and potash tube at the end of the experiment. The amount was found to be 0.15 g and 0.1837 g, respectively. The percentage of oxygen in compound A is %. (Nearest integer)
(Given: molar mass in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1} \mathrm{H}: 1, \mathrm{C}: 12, \mathrm{O}: 16$)
29652.sol:
In combustion analysis: CaCl₂ tube absorbs H₂O and potash tube absorbs CO₂.
Mass increase of CaCl₂ = 0.15 g gives moles of H₂O = 0.15/18 = 0.00833 mol, so moles of H = 0.01667 mol and mass of H = 0.01667 g.
Mass increase of potash = 0.1837 g gives moles of CO₂ = 0.1837/44 = 0.00417 mol, so moles of C = 0.00417 mol and mass of C = 0.05 g.
Mass of O = 0.25 - 0.05 - 0.01667 = 0.18333 g.
Percentage of O = (0.18333/0.25) × 100 = 73.33% ≈ 73% (nearest integer).

33342.text: Let $\alpha$ be the constant term in the binomial expansion of ${\left(\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{6}{x\dfrac{3}{2}}\right)}^{n}, n \le 15 .$ If the sum of the coefficients of the remaining terms in the expansion is $649$ and the coefficient of ${x}^{- n}$ is $\lambda\alpha,$ then $\lambda$ is equal to $________ .$
33342.sol:
Given,

${\left(\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{6}{x\dfrac{3}{2}}\right)}^{n}, n \le 15$

Now ${r}^{th}$ term is given by

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n {\left(x\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{n - r}{\left(- 6x\dfrac{- 3}{2}\right)}^{r}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = {\left(- 6\right)}^{r} \cdot Cr n \cdot x\dfrac{n - r}{2} \cdot x\dfrac{- 3r}{2}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = {\left(- 6\right)}^{r} \cdot Cr n \cdot x\dfrac{n - 4r}{2}$

Now we have to take, $n = 4r$ for constant term so $n$ is divisible by $4 .$

So, $\alpha = C\dfrac{n}{4} n \left(- 6\right)\dfrac{n}{4}$

And sum of all coefficients will be ${\left(\sqrt{1} - \dfrac{6}{1\dfrac{3}{2}}\right)}^{n} = {\left(- 5\right)}^{n}$

Also given, ${\left(- 5\right)}^{n} - C\dfrac{n}{4} n \left(- 6\right)\dfrac{n}{4} = 649$

Now by hit and trial we get, $n = 4$

Hence, $\alpha = C1 4 \left(- 6\right)\dfrac{4}{4} = - 24$

Now for coefficient of ${x}^{- 4}$

$\dfrac{n - 4r}{2} = - 4$

$⇒ n = 4r - 8 ⇒ r = 3$

So, $\lambda\left(\alpha\right) = {\left(- 6\right)}^{3} \cdot C3 4$

$⇒ \lambda\left(- 24\right) = {\left(- 6\right)}^{3} \cdot C3 4$

$⇒ \lambda = 36$

$⇒ a = 0, b = 9 ⇒ a + b = 9$

$∴ \dfrac{{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1}} = 9$

$∴ \sqrt{{h}_{1}{h}_{2}} = \left(\dfrac{{u}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}\right)\left(\dfrac{{u}^{2}\cos^{2}\theta}{2g}\right) = \dfrac{{u}^{2}sin\thetacos\theta}{2g}$$= \dfrac{R}{4}$

${⇒ R = 4\sqrt{{h}_{1}{h}_{2}}}^{}$

Hence, both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

47394.subject: Chemistry
47394.text: Basic strength of alkylamines in aqueous phase is not decided by ________.
47394.sol:
The basic strength of alkylamines in an aqueous solution is determined by the interplay of three main factors:

1. Inductive effect: The +I effect of alkyl groups increases the electron density on the nitrogen atom, making it more basic.
2. Solvation effect: The conjugate acid formed after accepting a proton is stabilized by hydrogen bonding with water molecules. Greater solvation leads to higher basicity.
3. Steric hindrance: Bulky alkyl groups can hinder the approach of a proton and also decrease the extent of solvation of the conjugate acid.

Hyperconjugation involves the delocalization of electrons from a filled $\sigma$ orbital to an adjacent empty or partially filled p-orbital or $\pi$ system. It does not play a role in determining the basic strength of alkylamines.

Answer: Hyperconjugation effect

Specific conductance is defined as the conductance of one centimeter cube (cc) of the solution of an electrolyte. Upon dilution, the concentration of ions per cc decreases, so the specific conductance falls.
Thus, specific conductance $\propto$ concentration of electrolytes, hence specific conductance is least for the solution of $0.002 \mathrm{ N}$ concentration.

55459.subject: Chemistry
55459.text: Which from following statements is NOT correct regarding tannins?
options: These avoid browning of freshly cut potato.
These are obtained by polymerisation of quinones.
These are generated after cutting fruits or vegetables.
55459.sol:
The browning process in plant tissues involves tannins and related phenolic compounds. When cells are damaged, enzymes oxidize these phenolics to quinones, which then polymerize into melanins. This mechanism indicates tannins are contributors to browning, not preventatives.

Tannins are polyphenolic compounds formed biosynthetically from simpler phenolic precursors, not from polymerization of quinones. Quinones are instead products of tannin oxidation during browning.

These compounds exist naturally in plant tissues prior to cutting; they are not generated afterward. Cutting merely releases them, facilitating enzymatic reactions.

Among the options, C inaccurately describes tannins as polymers of quinones, contradicting their true chemical nature and biosynthesis.

The correct identification is: $\boxed{C}$

55461.subject: Chemistry
55461.text: Which from following carbohydrates produces glucose, galactose and fructose on hydrolysis?
55461.sol:
Raffinose hydrolyzes to yield glucose, galactose, and fructose. As a trisaccharide, its hydrolysis reaction is $\text{Raffinose} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Glucose} + \text{Galactose} + \text{Fructose}$.

Maltose gives only glucose: $\text{Maltose} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Glucose}$. Cellulose produces glucose monomers: $(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5)_n + n\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow n\text{Glucose}$. Lactose yields glucose and galactose: $\text{Lactose} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Glucose} + \text{Galactose}$.

56820.text: What happens during the discharge of a lead storage battery?
56820.sol:
During the discharge of a lead storage battery, the following reactions take place:

At anode: $\text{Pb}(s) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2e^-$

At cathode: $\text{PbO}_2(s) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq) + 4\text{H}^+(aq) + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$

Overall reaction: $\text{Pb}(s) + \text{PbO}_2(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(aq) \rightarrow 2\text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$

From the overall cell reaction, it is clear that sulphuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) is consumed during the discharge process.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is consumed

57184.subject: Chemistry
57184.text: What is the number of structural isomers possible for alkene with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{10}$ ?
57184.sol:
The degree of unsaturation for $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{10}$ is determined by the formula $\text{DU} = x + 1 - \frac{y}{2}$ where $x = 5$ and $y = 10$. Substituting gives $\text{DU} = 5 + 1 - \frac{10}{2} = 1$, indicating one double bond.

Structural isomers with one carbon-carbon double bond and molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{10}$ are enumerated based on chain length and branching. The straight-chain isomers include pent-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$, and pent-2-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$.

Branched-chain isomers are derived from butene with methyl substitution: 2-methylbut-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$
3-methylbut-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_3$
and 2-methylbut-2-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$

This totals five structural isomers with no cyclic structures considered.

Final Answer: $\boxed{5}$

57988.subject: Chemistry
57988.text: Which of the following sentences is true for a basic solution?
options: In basic solution, the excess of $\text{OH}^-$ ions are present.
In the basic solution, there is excess of $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ ions.
The pOH of a basic solution can be calculated by pOH = $-\log[\text{H}^+]$
57988.sol:
In a neutral solution, $[\text{H}_3\text{O}^+] = [\text{OH}^-]$.

In an acidic solution, $[\text{H}_3\text{O}^+] > [\text{OH}^-]$, meaning there is an excess of $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ ions.

In a basic solution, $[\text{OH}^-] > [\text{H}_3\text{O}^+]$, meaning there is an excess of $\text{OH}^-$ ions.

The pOH of any solution is defined as $\text{pOH} = -\log[\text{OH}^-]$.

Thus, the only true statement is that in a basic solution, an excess of $\text{OH}^-$ ions are present.

Answer: In basic solution, the excess of $\text{OH}^-$ ions are present.

62822.subject: Mathematics
62822.text: The minimum value of $Z = 3x + y$, subject to the constraints $2x + 3y \leq 6, x + y \geq 1, x \geq 0, y \geq 0$ is....
62822.sol:
The objective function is $Z = 3x + y$.

The given constraints are:
$2x + 3y \leq 6$
$x + y \geq 1$
$x \geq 0, y \geq 0$

The feasible region is bounded by the lines $2x + 3y = 6$, $x + y = 1$, $x = 0$, and $y = 0$.

The corner points of the feasible region are the intersections of these lines with the coordinate axes:
For $x + y = 1$, the intercepts are $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$.
For $2x + 3y = 6$, the intercepts are $(3,0)$ and $(0,2)$.

Thus, the vertices of the feasible region are $(1,0)$, $(3,0)$, $(0,2)$, and $(0,1)$.

Evaluating $Z = 3x + y$ at each corner point:
At $(1,0)$: $Z = 3(1) + 0 = 3$
At $(3,0)$: $Z = 3(3) + 0 = 9$
At $(0,2)$: $Z = 3(0) + 2 = 2$
At $(0,1)$: $Z = 3(0) + 1 = 1$

The minimum value of $Z$ is $1$.

62926.subject: Mathematics
62926.text: The minimum number of switches in the simplified form of the following switching circuit is
62926.sol:
Let the switches $S_1, S_2, S_3$ be represented by boolean variables $p, q, r$ respectively. Then $S_1', S_2'$ represent their complements $p', q'$.

The given switching circuit consists of three parallel branches. We can write the boolean expression for the circuit as:
$L = (S_1 \cdot S_2) + (S_1' \cdot S_2) + (S_3 \cdot S_2')$

Substituting the variables, we get:
$L = (p \cdot q) + (p' \cdot q) + (r \cdot q')$

Now, we simplify the boolean expression:
Factor out $q$ from the first two terms:
$L = q \cdot (p + p') + r \cdot q'$

Since $p + p' = 1$ (a boolean variable and its complement always sum to 1):
$L = q \cdot 1 + r \cdot q'$
$L = q + q' \cdot r$

Using the distributive law $A + A'B = A + B$, we can further simplify:
$L = (q + q') \cdot (q + r)$
$L = 1 \cdot (q + r)$
$L = q + r$

Converting back to the switch notation, the simplified expression is:
$L = S_2 + S_3$

This simplified expression represents two switches (S_2$ and $S_3$) connected in parallel. Therefore, the minimum number of switches in the simplified form is 2$.

Answer: $2$

63156.subject: Mathematics
63156.text: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and if $A^2 - 2A + I = \begin{bmatrix} 18 & p \\ q & 11 \end{bmatrix}$, then $\ldots$
63156.sol:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$

First, we calculate $A^2$:
$A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 9 + 2 & -6 + 8 \\ -3 + 4 & 2 + 16 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 11 & 2 \\ 1 & 18 \end{bmatrix}$

Next, we calculate $2A$:
$2A = 2 \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -6 & 4 \\ 2 & 8 \end{bmatrix}$

Now, substituting these into $A^2 - 2A + I$:
$A^2 - 2A + I = \begin{bmatrix} 11 & 2 \\ 1 & 18 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} -6 & 4 \\ 2 & 8 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

$= \begin{bmatrix} 11 - (-6) + 1 & 2 - 4 + 0 \\ 1 - 2 + 0 & 18 - 8 + 1 \end{bmatrix}$

$= \begin{bmatrix} 18 & -2 \\ -1 & 11 \end{bmatrix}$

We are given that $A^2 - 2A + I = \begin{bmatrix} 18 & p \\ q & 11 \end{bmatrix}$.

Comparing the corresponding elements of the matrices, we get:
$p = -2$
$q = -1$

Answer: $p = -2,\ q = -1$

63575.subject: Mathematics
63575.text: If a random variable $X$ has a probability mass function $P(x) = \begin{cases} kx^2, & \text{for } x = 1, 2, 3, 4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$, then the mean of $X$ is...
63575.sol:
The sum of all probabilities must be equal to $1$.

$\sum_{x=1}^{4} P(x) = 1$

$k(1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 + 4^2) = 1$

$k(1 + 4 + 9 + 16) = 1$

$30k = 1 \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{1}{30}$

The mean of the random variable $X$ is given by $E(X) = \sum_{x=1}^{4} x P(x)$.

$E(X) = \sum_{x=1}^{4} x(kx^2) = k \sum_{x=1}^{4} x^3$

$E(X) = \dfrac{1}{30} (1^3 + 2^3 + 3^3 + 4^3)$

$E(X) = \dfrac{1}{30} (1 + 8 + 27 + 64)$

$E(X) = \dfrac{100}{30} = \dfrac{10}{3} = 3.333$

Answer: $3.333$

64096.text: The money invested in a company is compounded continuously. ₹400 invested today becomes $₹ 800$ in 6 years, then at the end of 33 years, it will become _{-}(\sqrt{2} =1 \cdot4142)
64096.sol:
Continuous compounding follows the formula $A = Pe^{rt}$, where $P$ is the principal, $r$ the annual rate, and $t$ the time in years.

To find $r$, set $P = 400$, $A = 800$, and $t = 6$:
$800 = 400e^{6r}$
$2 = e^{6r}$
Taking natural logarithms: $\ln(2) = 6r$, so $r = \frac{\ln(2)}{6}$.

For $t = 33$ years, with the same $P$ and $r$:
$A = 400e^{\left(\frac{\ln(2)}{6}\right) \cdot 33} = 400e^{5.5\ln(2)} = 400e^{\ln(2^{5.5})} = 400 \cdot 2^{5.5}$

Since $2^{5.5} = 2^5 \cdot 2^{0.5} = 32\sqrt{2} \approx 32 \cdot 1.4142 = 45.2544$,
$A = 400 \cdot 45.2544 = 18101.76$

This matches option B.

64100.sol: Let $\mathrm{AC}=\mathrm{n}, \mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{n}+1, \mathrm{BC}=\mathrm{n}+2\therefore \quad$ Largest angle is $\mathrm{A}$ and smallest angle is $\mathrm{B}$. \therefore \quad $\mathrm{A}=2 \mathrm{ B}$ Since $\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{C}=180^{{}^{\circ}}\therefore \quad 3 \mathrm{ B}+\mathrm{C}=180^{{}^{\circ}} \begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=180^{{}^{\circ}}-3 \mathrm{ B}\\ & \Rightarrow \sin \mathrm{C}=\sin \left(180^{{}^{\circ}}-3 \mathrm{ B}\right)=\sin3 \mathrm{ B} \end{aligned}$ By sine rule, $\begin{aligned}& \frac{\sin A}{n+2}=\frac{\sin B}{n}=\frac{\sin C}{n+1}\\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\sin 2 B}{n+2}=\frac{\sin B}{n}=\frac{\sin 3 B}{n+1}\\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2 \sin B \cos B}{n+2}=\frac{\sin B}{n}=\frac{3 \sin B-4 \sin ^3 B}{n+1}\\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2 \cos B}{n+2}=\frac{1}{n}=\frac{3-4 \sin ^2 B}{n+1}\\ \therefore & \cos B=\frac{n+2}{2 n},3-4 \sin ^2 B=\frac{n+1}{n}\\ \therefore \quad & 3-4\left(1-\cos ^2 B\right)=\frac{n+1}{n}\\ \therefore \quad & -4+4\left(\frac{n+2}{2 n}\right)^2=\frac{n+1}{n}\\ & \Rightarrow-1+\frac{n^2+4 n+4}{n^2}=\frac{n+1}{n}\\ & \Rightarrow-n²+n²+4 n+4=n²+n \\ & \Rightarrow n²-3 n-4=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(n+1)(n-4)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow n=-1 \text{$ or $} n=4 \end{aligned} But \mathrm{n}$ cannot be negative. \therefore $\mathrm{n}=4 $\therefore \quad$ The sides of the $\Delta$ are 4,5,6$.

66051.subject: Physics
66051.text: The earth is assumed to be a charged conducting sphere having volume 'V' and surface area 'A'. The capacitance of the earth in free space is (\epsilon_0$ = permittivity of free space)$
66051.sol:
The capacitance of a spherical conductor of radius $R$ is given by $C = 4\pi \epsilon_0 R$.

The volume of the sphere is $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3$ and its surface area is $A = 4\pi R^2$.

Taking the ratio of volume to surface area:

$\dfrac{V}{A} = \dfrac{\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3}{4\pi R^2} = \dfrac{R}{3}$

This gives $R = \dfrac{3V}{A}$.

Substituting the value of $R$ in the expression for capacitance:

$C = 4\pi \epsilon_0 \left(\dfrac{3V}{A}\right) = 12\pi \epsilon_0 \dfrac{V}{A}$

Answer: $12\pi \epsilon_0 V/A$

66354.subject: Physics
66354.text: To determine the internal resistance of a cell with potentiometer, when the cell is shunted by a resistance of $5 \Omega$, the balancing length is 250 cm. When the cell is shunted by $20 \Omega$, the balancing length of potentiometer wire is 400 cm. The internal resistance of the cell is
66354.sol:
The internal resistance $r$ of a cell using a potentiometer is determined by the formula $r = R \left( \frac{L_0}{L} -1\right)$, where $R$ is the external shunt resistance, $L_0$ is the balancing length for the cell's EMF in open circuit, and $L$ is the balancing length for the terminal potential difference.

Given two cases: with $R_1 = 5\,\Omega$ and $L_1 = 250\,\text{cm},$and $R_2 = 20\,\Omega$ and $L_2 = 400\,\text{cm},$the expressions for internal resistance are:

$r = 5 \left( \frac{L_0}{250} -1 \right)$

$r = 20 \left( \frac{L_0}{400} -1\right)$

Equating the two expressions:

$5 \left( \frac{L_0}{250} -1\right) = 20 \left( \frac{L_0}{400} -1 \right)$

Simplifying stepwise:

$\frac{L_0}{250} -1 = 4 \left( \frac{L_0}{400} -1\right)$

$\frac{L_0}{250} - 1 = \frac{L_0}{100} -4$

3 = L_0 $\left( \frac{1}{100} - \frac{1}{250} \right)$

3 = L_0 $\left( \frac{3}{500} \right)$

Solving for $L_0$ yields $L_0 = 500\,\text{cm}.$

Substituting into either expression for $r$:

$r = 5 \left( \frac{500}{250} -1\right) = 5 \Omega$

The internal resistance is $\boxed{5\,\Omega}$.

68142.subject: Physics
68142.text: The work done in splitting a water drop of radius $R$ in to 64 droplets is ( $\mathrm{T}=$ surface tension of water)
68142.sol:
Work done in splitting a water drop equals the increase in surface energy due to the change in surface area.

Given a large drop of radius $R$ splits into 64 smaller droplets, and volume is conserved: $V_{\text{large}} = 64 V_{\text{small}}$. Since volume scales as $R^3$, we have $R^3 = 64 r^3$, so $r = R/4$.

Initial surface area is $A_i = 4\pi R^2$. Final surface area is $A_f = 64 \cdot 4\pi r^2 = 256\pi r^2$. Substituting $r = R/4$ gives $A_f = 256\pi (R^2/16) = 16\pi R^2$.

Increase in surface area is $\Delta A = A_f - A_i = 16\pi R^2 - 4\pi R^2 = 12\pi R^2$.

Work done is $W = T \cdot \Delta A = 12\pi T R^2$.

$W = 12\pi T R^2$

A = maximum displacement of amplitude

Also, $v = a$ (given)

$⇒ \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \sqrt{3} \left[$∵ $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}\right]
$⇒ T = $\dfrac{2\pi}{\sqrt{3}}$ s

69169.subject: Physics
69169.text: Moment of inertia of a disc of mass $M$ and radius 'R' about any of its diameter is $MR^2/4$. The moment of inertia of this disc about an axis normal to the disc and passing through a point on its edge will be, $(x/2) MR^2$. The value of $x$ is
69169.sol:
Given the moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter is $I_{d} = \dfrac{MR^2}{4}$.

By the perpendicular axis theorem, the moment of inertia of the disc about an axis passing through its center and perpendicular to its plane is $I_{c} = I_{d} + I_{d} = \dfrac{MR^2}{4} + \dfrac{MR^2}{4} = \dfrac{MR^2}{2}$.

By the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of the disc about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through a point on its edge is $I = I_{c} + MR^2$.

Substituting the value of $I_{c}$, we get $I = \dfrac{MR^2}{2} + MR^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}MR^2$.

Comparing this with the given expression $\dfrac{x}{2}MR^2$, we get $x = 3$.

Answer: $3$

69187.subject: Physics
69187.text: Moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its diameter is 'I'. It is then casted into 27 small spheres of same diameter. The moment of inertia of each small sphere about its diameter is
69187.sol:
Given a solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ with moment of inertia $I = \frac{2}{5} M R^2$ about its diameter.

When recast into 27 smaller spheres of equal diameter, mass conservation gives $M = 27m$, so $m = \frac{M}{27}$.

Volume conservation implies $\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 27 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$, leading to $R^3 = 27r^3$ and $r = \frac{R}{3}$.

Each small sphere has moment of inertia $I' = \frac{2}{5} m r^2$.
Substituting $m = \frac{M}{27}$ and $r = \frac{R}{3}$,
this becomes $I' = \frac{2}{5} \left(\frac{M}{27}\right) \left(\frac{R}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{2}{5} M R^2 \times \frac{1}{243}$.

Recognizing $\frac{2}{5} M R^2 = I$, we obtain $I' = \frac{I}{243}$.

The moment of inertia of each small sphere about its diameter is $\frac{I}{243}$.

The correct answer is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

70888.subject: Biology
70888.text:
Match List I with List II
List I
(Types of stomata)		List II
(Group of plants where they occur)
(A). Epistomatic(I). Xerophytes
(B). Hypostomatic(II). Mesophytes
(C). Amphistomatic(III). Hydrophytes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
70888.sol:
Based on the distribution of stomata on the leaf surfaces, leaves are classified into different types that correlate with their ecological adaptations:

Epistomatic leaves have stomata exclusively on the upper (adaxial) epidermis. This adaptation is characteristic of floating hydrophytes (like water lilies), as their lower leaf surface is in contact with water and cannot facilitate direct gas exchange with the atmosphere. Thus, (A) matches with (III).

Hypostomatic leaves bear stomata mainly or entirely on the lower (abaxial) epidermis. This is the typical condition for dorsiventral leaves of dicotyledonous mesophytes, helping them minimize excessive transpirational water loss caused by direct exposure to sunlight. Thus, (B) matches with (II).

Amphistomatic leaves possess stomata on both the upper and lower surfaces. While found in monocot mesophytes, this is a very prominent adaptive feature of isobilateral leaves in many xerophytes. It allows them to maximize carbon dioxide uptake for photosynthesis during the brief periods when water is available and stomata are open. Thus, (C) matches with (I).

The correct matching sequence is (A) \rightarrow (III), (B) \rightarrow (II), and (C) \rightarrow (I).

Answer: (A) - (III), (B) - (II), (C) - (I)
70888.meta: Match List I with List II List I (Types of stomata) List II (Group of plants where they occur) (A). Epistomatic (I). Xerophytes (B). Hypostomatic (II).

71120.subject: Biology
71120.text:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I - Sporozoites of Plasmodium reproduce asexually to produce merozoites.
Statement II - Zygote of Plasmodium within the erythrocytes transforms into oocyst.
In the light of above statements, choose the correct option given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
71120.sol:
Statement I is correct because sporozoites of Plasmodium enter the human body through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito, reach the liver cells, and reproduce asexually (schizogony) to produce a large number of merozoites.

Statement II is incorrect because the zygote of Plasmodium is formed in the stomach (midgut) of the female Anopheles mosquito, not in human erythrocytes. The gametocytes are taken up by the mosquito during a blood meal, and fertilization occurs in its gut. The resulting zygote develops into a motile ookinete, which penetrates the gut wall and transforms into an oocyst.

Answer: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.

71806.subject: Chemistry
71806.text: The delocalization of electrons due to overlap between p-orbital and sigma bond is called.
71806.sol:
Hyperconjugation is the delocalization of electrons due to the overlap between a $\sigma$ bond (usually C-H or C-C) and an adjacent empty or partially filled p-orbital or a $\pi$-orbital.

Inductive effect involves the polarization of $\sigma$ bonds due to electronegativity differences.

Resonance involves the delocalization of $\pi$ electrons or lone pairs in parallel p-orbitals.

Therefore, the given description corresponds to hyperconjugation.

Answer: hyperconjugation

72144.text: A closed loop consists of a $15\ \text{V}$ battery, a $5\ \text{V}$ battery (opposing the first), and a $25\ \Omega$ resistor. The current through the loop is
72144.sol:
The net electromotive force in the loop is the difference between the two opposing batteries.

$E_{\text{net}} = 15 - 5 = 10\ \text{V}$

The total resistance in the loop is $R = 25\ \Omega$.

Using Ohm's law, the current $I$ is given by:

$I = \dfrac{E_{\text{net}}}{R} = \dfrac{10}{25} = 0.4\ \text{A}$

Answer: $0.4\ \text{A}$

79453.sol: Birds have remarkably specialized bones that are pneumatic because they are full of air sacs that provide a continuous flow of breath throughout their bodies. Also, it is one of the flight adaptations of the birds besides, lack of urinary bladder and boat-shaped body etc. E.g. Neophron (Vulture)

79487.subject: Botany
79487.text: Which of the following has notochord throughout life?
79487.sol: In Cephalochordates, the notochord is persistent throughout life, and Amphioxus or Lancelet is an example of Cephalochordata. In vertebrates, the notochord is present only during the embryonic stage. In Adults, the notochord is replaced by the vertebral column.

79583.subject: Botany
options: The walls of diatoms are easily destructible
'Diatomaceous earth' is formed by the cell walls of diatoms
Diatoms are chief producers in the oceans
Diatoms are microscopic and float passively in water
79583.sol: The cell walls of diatoms are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible. A unique feature of diatom cells is that they are enclosed within a cell wall made of hydrated silicon dioxide called a frustule. These frustules show a wide diversity in form but are usually almost bilaterally symmetrical, hence the group name diatom. The symmetry is not perfect since one of the valves is slightly larger than the other, allowing one valve to fit inside the edge of the other.

79803.text: The main organelle involved in modification and routing of newly synthesized proteins to their destinations is:
79803.sol: Endoplasmic reticulum, along with the Golgi apparatus, is involved in the transport of proteins and enzymes to their destination, i.e., within the cell and also outside the cell. Hence this is the right answer. While the lysosome is also involved in the transport of the hydrolytic enzymes, but it is not the major transport mechanism in the cell.

80585.subject: Botany
80585.text: What is the direction of micropyle in anatropous ovule?
80585.sol:
Anatropous ovule is the most common type of ovule found in angiosperms. Here the ovule is inverted so that micropyle and hilum are present in the same line and the micropyle is directed downwards.
Related Theory
Micropyle is used for the various functions and processes of the egg or the seed plant. It is located at top of the seed or egg. It helps in absorbing the water at the time of germination of the seed. Through micropyle the root emerges out at the time of germination of the seed.

80668.subject: Botany
80668.text: Opening and closing of stomata is due to the:
options: change in Turgor pressure of guard cells.
80668.sol:
The guard cells are filled with chloroplasts. The guard cells are rapidly influenced by changes in the turgor pressure that regulate the opening and closing of the stomata. In the case of dicot plants, the wall of the guard cells near the pore is thick and inelastic, whereas, the outer wall is thin, elastic and semi-permeable. When the turgor develops in the guard cells, the outer thin walls expand towards the outer side. This draws the thick inner walls slightly apart and creates a pore between the two guard cells. As a result, the stomata get opened. When the guard cells lose turgor due to the loss of water, the inner walls regain their original shape. The guard cells become flaccid and
the stoma closes.
Related Theory
Usually, the number of stomata is more on the lower surface of a dorsiventral leaf (dicot leaf) while the number of stomata is same on both the surfaces of leaf in isobilateral leaves (monocot leaves).

80997.subject: Chemistry
80997.text:
Given below is an expression for the rate constant of a first order reaction occurring at a certain temperature, $T$ (K).
$\ln k = 14.34 - \dfrac{1.25 \times 10^{4}}{T}$
The energy of activation in kcal mol$^{-1}$ for the reaction is :
(Given : $k$ in s$^{-1}$, $R = 1.987$ cal mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$)
80997.sol:
The Arrhenius equation is given by:

$\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{RT}$

The given equation is:

$\ln k = 14.34 - \dfrac{1.25 \times 10^{4}}{T}$

Comparing the two equations:

$\dfrac{E_a}{R} = 1.25 \times 10^{4}$

$E_a = 1.25 \times 10^{4} \times R$

Substituting $R = 1.987$ cal mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$:

$E_a = 1.25 \times 10^{4} \times 1.987$

$E_a = 24837.5$ cal mol$^{-1}$

$E_a = 24.8375$ kcal mol$^{-1} \approx 24.84$ kcal mol$^{-1}$

Answer: $24.84$

82615.text:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Electromagnetic wave)List II (Production)
A. MicrowaveI. Electrons in atoms emit light when they move from a higher energy level to a lower energy level

82615.sol:
Microwaves are produced by special vacuum tubes such as klystron valves, magnetron valves, and Gunn diodes. Thus, A matches IV.

Visible light is produced when electrons in atoms undergo transitions from a higher energy level to a lower energy level. Thus, B matches I.

Gamma rays are produced during the radioactive decay of the nucleus and other nuclear reactions. Thus, C matches II.

Infra-red rays are produced by hot bodies and molecules, specifically due to the vibration of atoms and molecules. Thus, D matches III.

The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

84413.subject: Zoology
84413.text: The maximum amount of electrolytes and water $(70-80 \%)$ from the glomerular filtrate is reabsorbed in which part of the nephron?
options: Ascending limb of loop of Henle
Descending limb of loop of Henle
84413.sol: From the Bowman's capsule, the glomerular filtrate enters the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT). PCT is surrounded by a network of peritubular capillaries and is the seat of reabsorption. About $75 \%$ of glomerular filtrate is normally reabsorbed in PCT before reaching the loop of Henle. The reabsorbed materials include glucose, amino acids, vitamins, hormones, sodium, potassium, chlorides, phosphates, bicarbonates, most of water and some urea etc.

84510.subject: Zoology
84510.text: Cirrhosis of liver is caused by the chronic intake of
84510.sol: The chronic intake of alcohol may be fatal for the individual. On intake, a part of alcohol is changed to acetaldehyde which causes hangover. Acetaldehyde stimulates formation of fat which is deposited on artery walls (causing coronary ailments) and in the liver (causing fatty liver syndrome). Gradually, the liver hardens and dries up as its cells are replaced by fibrous tissue. This kind of liver degeneration is called liver cirrhosis (Laennec's cirrhosis). Excessive use of alcohol may also lead liver failure, liver cell carcinoma, etc.

85406.subject: Zoology
85406.text: The test-tube baby programme employs which one of the following techniques?
85406.sol: The test-tube baby programme employs the technique of in vitro fertilization (IVF) and zygote intrafallopian transfer (ZIFT) technique. ZIFT is a method used to treat infertility, in which an egg fertilized in vitro (outside the body) is placed into a woman's fallopian tube (oviduct). It is an assisted reproductive procedure similar to IVF and embryo transfer, the difference being that zygote or proembryo is transferred into the fallopian tube, instead of the uterus. Because the fertilized egg (zygote) is directly transferred into the tubes, the procedure is also referred to as tubal embryo transfer.

Heliconius butterflies avoid laying eggs on those leaves that already have eggs or yellow spots ensuring hatching of fewer caterpillars per leaf. $y + 7 = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x + 9\right)$
$x + 2y + 23 = 0 . . . ( ii )$
The point $Q$ is the intersection of the tangent at $P$ and the normal at $Q$

On solving the equation $( i ) \text{ and } ( ii )$, we get,

$x + 2\left(2x + 4\right) + 23 = 0$

$⇒ 5x = - 31 ⇒ x = - \dfrac{31}{5}$

and $y = 2\left(- \dfrac{31}{5}\right) + 4 = - \dfrac{42}{5}$

Hence, the coordinates of the point $Q$ are $\left(- \dfrac{31}{5}, - \dfrac{42}{5}\right)$

92543.text: A stationary hydrogen atom in the first excited state emits a photon. If the mass of the hydrogen atom is $m$ and its ionization energy is $E$, then the recoil velocity acquired by the atom is [speed of light = $c$]
92543.sol:
$mv = \dfrac{h}{λ}$, here $v$~is recoil& speed of $H$-atom and~$\lambda$~is the wavelength of the photon.

When the electron jumps down from the first excited state to the ground state the energy released is

$∆ {E}_{2 \to 1} = E\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{22}\right) = \dfrac{3E}{4}$

$\dfrac{3E}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{hc}{λ}$

$\dfrac{3E}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + mvc$

~$\left(\dfrac{m}{2}\right)v^{2} + \left(mc\right)v - \left(\dfrac{3E}{4}\right) = 0$

$⇒ v = \left[\sqrt{\dfrac{3E}{2m} + c^{2}}\right] - c$

92623.text: A body of mass $3kg$ collides elastically with another body at rest and then continues to move in the original direction with one-half of its original speed. What is the mass of the target body (in $kg$)?
92623.sol:
Conservation of linear momentum :
$3u = ( 3u / 2 ) + mv ⇒ mv = ( 3u / 2 ) \ldots ( 1 )$



Newton's experimental law :
$u = – e ( u / 2 – v )$

Putting $e = 1$ for elastic collision we obtain,
$v = \dfrac{3u}{2} \ldots . . ( 2 )$
Using (1) and (2), we obtain $m = 1kg$.

93035.text: Electromagnetic waves travel in a medium with a speed of $\text{2} \times {\text{10}^{8} \text{m}s^{- 1}.$ The relative permeability of the medium is $1$. Find the relative permittivity.
93035.sol:
Here, $\text{v} = 2 \times {10}^{8} \text{m}s^{- 1}$ and ${μ}_{r} = 1$

The speed of electromagnetic waves in a medium is given by

$\text{v} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\text{\mu} \text{ε}}} \text{,} \text{....(i)}$

where $\mu$ and $ε$ are absolute permeability and absolute permittivity of the medium.

Now, $\mu = {μ}_{0} {μ}_{r}$ and $ε = {ε}_{0} {ε}_{r}$

Therefore, the equation (i) becomes

$\text{v} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{μ}_{0} {μ}_{r} \times {ε}_{0} {ε}_{r}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{μ}_{0} {ε}_{0}}} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{μ}_{r} {ε}_{r}}} = \dfrac{\text{c}}{\sqrt{{μ}_{r} {ε}_{r}}}$

$\text{or} {ε}_{r} = \dfrac{c^{2}}{v^{2} {μ}_{r}} = \dfrac{{\left(3 \times {10}^{8}\right)}^{2}}{{\left(2 \times {10}^{8}\right)}^{2} \times 1} = \text{2.25}$

Respiration is the process or mechanism to break down food molecules to release energy in the form of ATP. 101425.subject: Physics
101425.text: A geostationary satellite orbits the Earth at a radial distance $R_G$ from the Earth's centre. Another artificial satellite orbits the Earth in a circular orbit of radius $\dfrac{R_G}{4}$. What is the time period of this second satellite?
101425.sol:
The time period of a geostationary satellite is $T_1 = 24 \text{ hours}$.

According to Kepler's Third Law, the square of the time period is proportional to the cube of the orbital radius, i.e., $T^2 \propto r^3$.

For the two satellites, we can write:
$\left(\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}\right)^3$

Taking the square root on both sides:
$\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = \left(\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}\right)^{3/2}$

Given $r_1 = R_G$ and $r_2 = \dfrac{R_G}{4}$:
$\dfrac{T_2}{24} = \left(\dfrac{R_G / 4}{R_G}\right)^{3/2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{3/2} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$T_2 = \dfrac{24}{8} = 3 \text{ hours}$.

Answer: $3 \text{ hours}$

102005.subject: Physics
102005.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If heat is added to a system, its temperature must increase.

Statement II: If positive work is done by a system in a thermodynamic process, its volume must increase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
102005.sol:
If heat energy is added to a thermodynamic system, one part increases the internal energy and the other part performs some work.

If heat is added to a system, the system can do work without changing its internal energy. Hence, statement 1 is false.

The formula to calculate the work done is given by

$W = ∫ PdV$

From the above equation, it can be concluded that if $W > 0$, i.e., work is done by the system, its volume must increase. Hence, statement II is true.

102072.subject: Physics
102072.text: An ideal gas of $n$ moles is taken from state 1 to state 2. On a pressure-temperature ($P-T$) diagram, this process is represented by a straight line passing through the origin. If the temperature of the gas changes from $T_1$ to $T_2$, the work done by the gas is:
102072.sol:
According to the ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$, which can be rearranged as $P = \left(\dfrac{nR}{V}\right)T$.

The process is given as a straight line passing through the origin on the $P-T$ diagram. The equation of such a line is $P = kT$, where $k$ is a constant slope.

Comparing the two equations, we get $\dfrac{nR}{V} = k$. Since $n$, $R$, and $k$ are constants, the volume $V$ must also be constant.

A process where the volume remains constant is an isochoric process ($\Delta V = 0$).

The work done by a gas is given by $W = \int P \, dV$. Since there is no change in volume, the work done by the gas is zero.

Answer: Zero

102423.subject: Physics
102423.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If a small mass placed on an oscillating horizontal block is suddenly lifted off vertically when the block is exactly at its extreme position, the amplitude of oscillation of the remaining block remains unchanged.
Reason (R): At the extreme position, the magnitude of the restoring force acting on the oscillating system is maximum.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
102423.sol:
At the extreme position, the velocity of the oscillating system is zero. When the small mass is lifted off, it takes away zero kinetic energy. The remaining block still has zero kinetic energy and the spring is at the same maximum extension, meaning the potential energy $\dfrac{1}{2}kA^2$ is unchanged. Since the total mechanical energy of the remaining system is conserved and depends only on the spring constant $k$ and the amplitude, the new amplitude must equal the old amplitude. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.

The restoring force in simple harmonic motion is given by $F = -kx$. At the extreme position, the displacement $x$ is maximum (equal to the amplitude), so the magnitude of the restoring force is indeed maximum. Thus, Reason (R) is true.

However, the fact that the restoring force is maximum does not explain why the amplitude remains unchanged. The correct explanation is based on the fact that kinetic energy is zero at the extreme position, so removing mass does not alter the total mechanical energy. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

103688.subject: Physics
103688.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When an electron is projected in the direction of parallel uniform electric and magnetic fields, its kinetic energy decreases but its path remains a straight line.

Reason (R): The magnetic force on the electron is zero, and the electric force acts in the direction of its velocity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
103688.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: When an electron is projected parallel to the magnetic field, the angle between its velocity and the magnetic field is zero. The magnetic force is $F_m = qvB\sin(0^\circ) = 0$, so the magnetic field does not deflect it, and the path remains a straight line. However, the electron is negatively charged, so the electric force $\vec{F}_e = -e\vec{E}$ acts in the direction opposite to the electric field (and thus opposite to its initial velocity). This opposing force causes the electron to decelerate, decreasing its kinetic energy.

Reason (R) is false: While it is true that the magnetic force on the electron is zero, the electric force acts opposite to the direction of its velocity, not in the direction of its velocity.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

104253.subject: Physics
104253.text: An electromagnetic wave travelling in a vacuum has a frequency of $3 \times 10^{13}\text{ Hz}$. What is the wavelength of this wave, and to which region of the electromagnetic spectrum does it belong?
104253.sol:
The relationship between the speed of light ($c$), frequency ($ u$), and wavelength ($\lambda$) is given by:
$c = u \lambda$

Given:
Frequency, $ u = 3 imes 10^{13} ext{ Hz}$
Speed of light in vacuum, $c = 3 imes 10^8 ext{ m/s}$

Rearranging the formula to solve for wavelength:
$\lambda = \dfrac{c}{ u}$
$\lambda = \dfrac{3 imes 10^8}{3 imes 10^{13}}$
$\lambda = 10^{-5} ext{ m}$

According to the electromagnetic spectrum, the wavelength range from $10^{-3} ext{ m}$ to $7 imes 10^{-7} ext{ m}$ corresponds to Infrared rays. Therefore, a wavelength of $10^{-5} ext{ m}$ falls in the infrared region.

Multiplying the values instead of dividing leads to the incorrect $9 imes 10^{21} ext{ m}$, and confusing the spectrum ranges leads to incorrectly identifying it as ultraviolet or microwaves.

Answer: $10^{-5} ext{ m}$, Infrared rays

104807.sol:
- Assertion (A): In the Davisson-Germer experiment, the wavelength associated with the electron beam indeed decreases with the increase in the speed of electrons. This follows from de Broglie's equation, \(\lambda=$\frac{h}{m v}$\), where \(v\) is the speed of the electrons. As the speed increases, the wavelength decreases, making the assertion true.
- Reason (R): The equation \(\lambda=$\frac{h}{2 m K}$\) is incorrect. The correct form of de Broglie's wavelength is \(\lambda=$\frac{h}{p}$\) where \(p=m v\) is the momentum of the electron, or \(\lambda=$\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m E_k}}$\), where \(E_k\) is the kinetic energy of the electron.

104877.subject: Physics
104877.text:
An electron in a singly ionized helium atom (He$^+$) has a potential energy of $-6.8$ eV. The radial distance of the electron from the nucleus in this state is approximately :
(Take $1$ eV $= 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ J, $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C and $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^{9}$ N m$^2$/C$^2$)
104877.sol:
The potential energy $U$ of an electron in a hydrogen-like ion is given by:
$U = -\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{Z e^2}{r}$

For a singly ionized helium atom (He$^+$), the atomic number $Z = 2$.
The given potential energy is $U = -6.8$ eV. Converting this to Joules:
$U = -6.8 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ J

Equating the two expressions for potential energy:
$-6.8 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = -\dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 2 \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})^2}{r}$

Dividing both sides by $-1.6 \times 10^{-19}$:
$6.8 = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 2 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{r}$

$6.8 = \dfrac{28.8 \times 10^{-10}}{r}$

$r = \dfrac{28.8 \times 10^{-10}}{6.8}$

$r \approx 4.235 \times 10^{-10}$ m

This is approximately $4.2 \times 10^{-10}$ m.

Answer: $4.2 \times 10^{-10}$ m

105222.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A p-n junction diode with its p-side connected to $-2\text{ V}$ and its n-side connected to $-5\text{ V}$ is forward-biased.
Reason (R): For a diode to be forward-biased, both the p-side and the n-side must be at positive potentials.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
105222.sol:
For a p-n junction diode to be forward-biased, the potential at the p-side must be greater than the potential at the n-side ($V_p > V_n$).

In the Assertion, $V_p = -2\text{ V}$ and $V_n = -5\text{ V}$. Since $-2\text{ V} > -5\text{ V}$, the diode is forward-biased. Thus, Assertion (A) is correct.

The Reason states that both sides must be at positive potentials for forward bias. This is incorrect, as forward bias only depends on the relative potential difference ($V_p > V_n$), which can be achieved even if both potentials are negative, as demonstrated in the Assertion. Thus, Reason (R) is incorrect.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect

105248.subject: Physics
105248.text: In a standard center-tap full-wave rectifier circuit, diodes $D_1$ and $D_2$ are connected to the upper and lower ends of the secondary coil respectively. The input AC voltage is given by $V = V_0 \sin(50\pi t)$. At a certain instant of time $t$, it is observed that diode $D_1$ is reverse biased and diode $D_2$ is forward biased. Which of the following could be a possible value of time $t$?
105248.sol:
The input voltage is $V = V_0 \sin(50\pi t)$.

The angular frequency is $\omega = 50\pi \text{ rad/s}$, so the time period of the AC input is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{2\pi}{50\pi} = 0.04 \text{ s} = 40 \text{ ms}$.

During the positive half-cycle ($0 < t < 20 \text{ ms}$), the upper end of the secondary is positive, making $D_1$ forward biased and $D_2$ reverse biased.

During the negative half-cycle ($20 \text{ ms} < t < 40 \text{ ms}$), the upper end is negative and the lower end is positive, making $D_1$ reverse biased and $D_2$ forward biased.

At $t = 20 \text{ ms}$, the voltage is zero, so neither diode conducts.

At $t = 45 \text{ ms}$, the cycle repeats and it is again in the positive half-cycle.

Therefore, the time $t$ must lie between $20 \text{ ms}$ and $40 \text{ ms}$. Among the given options, $35 \text{ ms}$ is the only possible value.

Answer: $35 \text{ ms}$

107786.subject: Chemistry
107786.text: Which of the following molecules contains exactly two $\pi$ bonds and has carbon atoms in both $sp$ and $sp^2$ hybridization states, but no $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom?
107786.sol:
Let us analyze the given molecules for their number of $\pi$ bonds and the hybridization of their carbon atoms:

Propyne ($CH_3-C \equiv CH$): Contains one triple bond, hence two $\pi$ bonds. The carbon atoms are $sp^3$, $sp$, and $sp$ hybridized. It contains an $sp^3$ carbon, so it does not match the criteria.

Buta-1,3-diene ($CH_2=CH-CH=CH_2$): Contains two double bonds, hence two $\pi$ bonds. All four carbon atoms are $sp^2$ hybridized. It lacks an $sp$ hybridized carbon.

Propadiene ($CH_2=C=CH_2$): Contains two double bonds, hence two $\pi$ bonds. The terminal carbons are $sp^2$ hybridized and the central carbon is $sp$ hybridized. It contains no $sp^3$ carbon. This perfectly matches all criteria.

But-1-en-3-yne ($CH_2=CH-C \equiv CH$): Contains one double bond and one triple bond, hence three $\pi$ bonds. The carbons are $sp^2$, $sp^2$, $sp$, and $sp$ hybridized. It has too many $\pi$ bonds.

Answer: Propadiene

111886.subject: Chemistry
111886.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The cycloheptatrienyl (tropylium) cation is exceptionally stable compared to typical alkyl carbocations.

options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
111886.sol:
Assertion (A) is true. The cycloheptatrienyl (tropylium) cation is exceptionally stable because it is an aromatic carbocation.

Reason (R) is false. While the tropylium cation does contain six $\pi$ electrons ($4n+2$ where $n=1$), a strict requirement for aromaticity according to Hückel's rule is that the ring must be planar to allow for continuous delocalization of the $\pi$ electrons. The reason incorrectly states that the ring is non-planar.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false.

113902.subject: Chemistry
113902.text: Two aqueous solutions, A and B, are observed to boil at the same temperature. Solution A is $0.1 \text{ M } \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$ and Solution B is $0.2 \text{ M}$ of a weak monoprotic acid $\mathrm{HX}$. Assuming molality is approximately equal to molarity, the degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) of the weak acid $\mathrm{HX}$ is:
113902.sol:
For solutions to boil at the same temperature, their elevation in boiling point ($\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}}$) must be equal.

$\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}} = i \cdot \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}} \cdot m$

Assuming $m \approx \mathrm{M}$, we equate the effective concentrations ($i \times \mathrm{M}$) of both solutions.

For $\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$ (a strong electrolyte), $i = 3$.
Effective concentration of A = $3 \times 0.1 = 0.3 \text{ M}$.

For the weak monoprotic acid $\mathrm{HX}$, $i = 1 + \alpha$.
Effective concentration of B = $(1 + \alpha) \times 0.2 \text{ M}$.

Equating the two:
$(1 + \alpha) \times 0.2 = 0.3$
$1 + \alpha = 1.5$
$\alpha = 0.5$

Percentage degree of dissociation = $0.5 \times 100 = 50\%$.

If the van 't Hoff factor of $\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$ is incorrectly taken as 2, it leads to $25\%$. If the formula for $i$ is misapplied as just $\alpha$, it leads to $150\%$.

Answer: $50\%$

113910.subject: Chemistry
113910.text: When chloroform and acetone are mixed, they form a non-ideal solution. Which of the following statements correctly describes this mixture?
options: The intermolecular attractive forces between chloroform and acetone are stronger than those in the pure liquids, and $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H < 0$.
The intermolecular attractive forces between chloroform and acetone are weaker than those in the pure liquids, and $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V > 0$.
The mixture exhibits a positive deviation from Raoult's law, and $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H > 0$.
The intermolecular attractive forces remain unchanged upon mixing, and $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0$.
113910.sol:
When chloroform and acetone are mixed, a hydrogen bond is formed between the hydrogen atom of chloroform and the oxygen atom of acetone. This new intermolecular interaction (solute-solvent) is stronger than the interactions present in the pure liquids (solute-solute and solvent-solvent).

As a result, the escaping tendency of the molecules decreases, leading to a lower vapour pressure than expected from Raoult's law. This is termed a negative deviation.

For solutions showing a negative deviation from Raoult's law, the mixing process is exothermic ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}H < 0$) and is accompanied by a decrease in volume ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}V < 0$).

Answer: The intermolecular attractive forces between chloroform and acetone are stronger than those in the pure liquids, and $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H < 0$.

The value of $\Lambda_m$ for a $0.04$ M aqueous solution of $\text{MX}_2$ at $298$ K is:
114389.sol:
According to Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions, the limiting molar conductivity of $\text{MX}_2$ is:

$\Lambda_m^0(\text{MX}_2) = \lambda^0_{\text{M}^{2+}} + 2\lambda^0_{\text{X}^-}$

$\Lambda_m^0 = 120.0 + 2(60.0) = 240.0$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$

For a strong electrolyte, the Debye-Huckel-Onsager equation is:

$\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^0 - A\sqrt{c}$

The slope of the $\Lambda_m$ versus $\sqrt{c}$ plot is $-A$. Given the slope is $-100.0$, we have $A = 100.0$.

At concentration $c = 0.04$ M, $\sqrt{c} = \sqrt{0.04} = 0.2$ M$^{1/2}$.

Substituting the values into the equation:

$\Lambda_m = 240.0 - (100.0 \times 0.2)$

$\Lambda_m = 240.0 - 20.0 = 220.0$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$

Answer: $220.0$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$

118258.subject: Chemistry
118258.text: Which of the following alkyl halides will undergo hydrolysis via the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ mechanism at the fastest rate and yield a racemic mixture?
118258.sol:
For an alkyl halide to yield a racemic mixture upon $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ hydrolysis, the starting compound must be chiral. For the reaction to occur at the fastest rate, it should form the most stable carbocation (e.g., a tertiary carbocation).

2-Bromo-2-methylbutane is a tertiary alkyl halide but it is achiral (the carbon bearing the bromine atom is attached to two identical methyl groups). It will undergo $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ fast but cannot yield a racemic mixture as it is not optically active.

2-Bromobutane is a chiral secondary alkyl halide. It will yield a racemic mixture but its $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ rate is slower than that of a tertiary halide.

1-Bromobutane is a primary alkyl halide and is achiral. It prefers the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ mechanism.

3-Bromo-3-methylhexane is a tertiary alkyl halide and is chiral (the chiral center is attached to a bromine atom, a methyl group, an ethyl group, and a propyl group). It forms a highly stable tertiary carbocation, leading to the fastest $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ rate, and yields a racemic mixture.

Answer: 3-Bromo-3-methylhexane

118259.subject: Chemistry
118259.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Bromobenzene does not yield $\alpha$-bromophenylacetic acid when subjected to the reaction sequence of KCN, followed by acidic hydrolysis, and then $\text{Br}_2$/Red P.
Reason (R): Aryl halides are highly unreactive towards nucleophilic substitution reactions under normal conditions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
118259.sol:
The Assertion is correct. The proposed reaction sequence begins with the treatment of bromobenzene with KCN. However, this first step fails because the C-Br bond in bromobenzene acquires partial double bond character due to resonance, making it highly resistant to nucleophilic substitution by the cyanide ion under normal conditions.

Since the first step (formation of benzonitrile) does not occur, the subsequent steps cannot proceed to form $\alpha$-bromophenylacetic acid.

The Reason is also correct and provides the exact explanation for why the reaction described in the Assertion does not take place. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

121757.text: What type of sexual reproduction is found in red algae?
121757.sol: The members of rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae because of the predominance of the red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body. Majority of the red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas. They occur in both well-lighted regions close to the surface of water and also at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates.The red thalli of most of the red algae are multicellular. Some of them have complex body organization. The food is stored as floridean starch which is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure. The red algae usually reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation. They reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes. <mark>Sexual reproduction is oogamous and accompanied by complex post fertilization developments.</mark> The common members are: Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria and Gelidium.

121879.sol: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. They are also frequently grown as ornamentals. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. You may recall that in bryophytes the dominant phase in the life cycle is the gametophytic plant body. However, in pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves (Figure 3.3). These organs possess well-differentiated vascular tissues. The leaves in pteridophytes are small (microphylls) as in Selaginella or large (macrophylls) as in ferns.

122200.subject: Botany
122200.text: What is the level of organization in cnidarians?
122200.sol: Cnidoblasts, also known as cnidocytes, contain stinging capsules or nematocysts and are used for anchorage, defense, and prey capture in cnidarians. Cnidarians exhibit tissue level of organization and are diploblastic.They have a central gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening, mouth on hypostome. Digestion is extracellular and intracellular. Some of the cnidarians, e.g., corals have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate. Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa (Figure 4.6). The former is a sessile and cylindrical form like Hydra, Adamsia, etc. whereas, the latter is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming like Aurelia or jelly fish. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (Metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia).

125615.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Pigments that appear yellow and yellow-orange on a paper chromatogram are crucial for protecting chlorophyll $a$ from photo-oxidation.
Reason (R): These pigments absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll $a$, acting as accessory pigments.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
125615.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: Pigments that appear yellow (xanthophylls) and yellow to yellow-orange (carotenoids) on a paper chromatogram are accessory pigments. One of their crucial functions is to protect chlorophyll $a$ from photo-oxidation.

Reason (R) is correct: These pigments also absorb light of different wavelengths and transfer the energy to chlorophyll $a$, which broadens the spectrum of light used for photosynthesis.

However, (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). The fact that they transfer energy to chlorophyll $a$ is a separate parallel function and does not explain the mechanism by which they protect chlorophyll $a$ from photo-oxidation. 125865.subject: Botany
125865.text: What type of flowers do not open at all?
125865.sol: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower. In a nomal flower which opens and exposes the anthers and the stigma, complete autogamy is rather rare. Autogamy in such flowers requires synchrony in pollen release and stigma receptivity and also, the anthers and the stigma should. lie close to each other so that self-pollination can occur. Some plants such as Viola (common pansy), Oxalis, and Commelina produce two types of flowers – chasmogamous flowers which are similar to flowers of other species with exposed anthers and stigma, and cleistogamous flowers which do not open at all. In such flowers, the anthers and stigma lie close to each other. When anthers dehisce in the flower buds, pollen grains come in contact with the stigma to effect pollination.

125919.subject: Botany
125919.text: What is the pistil’s role if it detects incompatible pollen?
options: Prevents pollen germination or tube growth
Facilitates the entry of pollen into the ovule
125919.sol: Pollen-pistil Interaction : Pollination does not guarantee the transfer of the right type of pollen (compatible pollen of the same species as the stigma). The pistil has the ability to recognise the pollen, whether it is of the right type (compatible) or of the wrong type (incompatible). If it is of the right type, the pistil accepts the pollen and promotes post-pollination events that leads to fertilisation. If the pollen is of the wrong type, the pistil rejects the pollen by preventing pollen germination on the stigma or the pollen tube growth in the style. The ability of the pistil to recognise the pollen followed by its acceptance or rejection is the result of a continuous dialogue between pollen grain and the pistil. This dialogue is mediated by chemical components of the pollen interacting with those of the pistil.

126512.text: Why are competitive inhibitors often used to control bacterial pathogens?
options: To increase the activity of enzymes
To decrease the activity of enzymes
To maintain the activity of enzymes
126512.sol: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor. Due to its close structural similarity with the substrate, the inhibitor competes with the substrate for the substrate-binding site of the enzyme. Consequently, the substrate cannot bind and as a result, the enzyme action declines, e.g., inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate which closely resembles the substrate succinate in structure. Such competitive inhibitors are often used in the control of bacterial pathogens.

127548.text: What is the main cause for the extinction of some species in tropical forest ?
127548.sol: Deforestation is the depletion of forest resources. Its main cause is the explosion of human and livestock population with the increased demand of the basic needs. Ideally one third ( $33 \%$ ) of land of a country must be covered by forest. In India forest cover is only $19.43 \%$ out of which only $13 \%$ are thick forest. 128094.text:

Assertion (A): Cockroach is a uricotelic animal.

options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
128094.sol:
According to NCERT, cockroaches excrete nitrogenous waste primarily in the form of uric acid, which makes them uricotelic animals. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.

The Malpighian tubules are the principal excretory organs in cockroaches. They absorb nitrogenous waste products from the haemolymph and convert them into uric acid, not urea. This uric acid is then excreted out through the hindgut. Thus, Reason (R) is false.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

129058.subject: Zoology
129058.text: A doctor administers anti-Rh antibodies to a woman immediately after the delivery of her first child to protect her future pregnancies. Based on this medical intervention, what must be the Rh blood group status of the mother and her newborn?
options: Mother is Rh-positive and newborn is Rh-negative
Both mother and newborn are Rh-negative
Both mother and newborn are Rh-positive
Mother is Rh-negative and newborn is Rh-positive
129058.sol:
Erythroblastosis foetalis is a condition caused by Rh incompatibility when an Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive foetus.

During the delivery of the first child, the maternal blood may be exposed to a small amount of the Rh-positive blood from the foetus. This exposure causes the mother's immune system to start preparing anti-Rh antibodies, which could cross the placenta and destroy the foetal red blood cells in subsequent pregnancies.

To prevent this sensitization, anti-Rh antibodies are administered to the Rh-negative mother immediately after the delivery of her Rh-positive child. This destroys any foetal Rh antigens in her bloodstream before her immune system can react to them.

Answer: Mother is Rh-negative and newborn is Rh-positive

129713.text:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Nephron Segment)List II (Feature/Function)
A. Proximal convoluted tubuleI. Simple cuboidal brush border epithelium
B. Descending limb of Henle's loopII. Simple columnar brush border epithelium
C. Ascending limb of Henle's loopIII. Permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes

129713.sol:
The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) is lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium which increases the surface area for reabsorption (A matches I).

The descending limb of loop of Henle is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes, which concentrates the filtrate as it moves down (B matches III).

The ascending limb is impermeable to water but allows transport of electrolytes actively or passively (C matches IV).

The distal convoluted tubule (DCT) is capable of conditional reabsorption of Na$^+$ and water (D matches V).

Simple columnar brush border epithelium (II) is not found in these segments; it is typically found in the intestine.

Answer: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-V

Carbon dioxide (CO2) which is harmful is also released during the above catabolic reactions. It is, therefore, evident that O2 has to be continuously provided to the cells and CO2 produced by the cells have to be released out. This process of exchange of O2 from the atmosphere with CO2 produced by the cells is called breathing, commonly known as respiration. 131665.sol: DNA as an acidic substance present in nucleus was first identified by Friedrich Meischer in 1869. He named it ‘Nuclein’. However, due to technical limitations in isolating such a long polymer intact, the elucidation of structure of DNA remained elusive for a very long period of time. It was only in 1953 that James Watson and Francis Crick, based on the X-ray diffraction data produced by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin,proposed a very simple but famous Double Helix model for the structure of DNA. One of the hallmarks of their proposition was base pairing between the two strands of polynucleotide chains. However, this proposition is also based on the observation of Erwin Chargaff that for a double stranded DNA, the ratios between Adenine and Thymine and Guanine and Cytosine are constant and equals one.

132138.subject: Zoology
132138.text: What is a good example of co-dominance mentioned in the paragraph?
132138.sol: in the case of co-dominance the F1 generation resembles both parents. A good example is different types of red blood cells that determine ABO blood grouping in human beings. ABO blood groups are controlled by the gene I. The plasma membrane of the red blood cells has sugar polymers that protrude from its surface and the kind of sugar is controlled by the gene. The gene (I) has three alleles I A , I B and i. The alleles I A and I B produce a slightly different form of the sugar while allele i does not produce any sugar. Because humans are diploid organisms, each person possesses any two of the three I gene alleles. I A and I B are completely dominant over i, in other words when I A and i are present only I A expresses (because i does not produce any sugar), and when I B and i are present I B expresses. But when I A and I B are present together they both express their own types of sugars: this is because of co-dominance. Hence red blood cells have both A and B types of sugars. Since there are three different alleles, there are six different combinations of these three alleles that are possible, and therefore, a total of six different genotypes of the human ABO blood types
